places.name: Kokiri Forest
places.intro: Kokiri Forest, the village where the adventure begins, has three Gold Skulltulas and the soft soil for a Magic Bean on its map. Two of the Skulltulas appear as a child: the one behind the House of the Know-It-All Brothers, only at night, and the one in the soft soil by the shop, at any hour and with Bugs. Plant a bean in that same patch too, because as an adult it lifts you to a ledge with Rupees, and come back at night with the Hookshot for the third Skulltula, on top of the House of the Twins.

places.name: Lost Woods
places.intro: Almost everything in the Lost Woods is collected as a child: two Pieces of Heart with the ocarina, three Gold Skulltulas and two patches for Magic Beans. It's the maze that links Kokiri Forest with the Sacred Forest Meadow, and the Pieces are down to the Skull Kids: Saria's Song for the one with the flute, left of the entrance, and the memory game by the target, to the right. Bring Bugs for the two patches of soft soil, the one by the bridge to Hyrule Field and the one in the lone-tree clearing, and plant a bean in each: as an adult and at night, the one in the clearing lifts you to the ledge of the third Skulltula.

places.name: Sacred Forest Meadow
places.intro: A single Gold Skulltula, and as an adult, is all the Sacred Forest Meadow holds, and the map marks where it appears in the maze leading to the Forest Temple. It shows up on the right-hand wall halfway through the maze, after you dodge the Moblins and before the staircase: knock it down with the Hookshot, the same one you need to enter the temple.

places.name: Hyrule Field
places.intro: The Hyrule Field map marks two Pieces of Heart and two Gold Skulltulas. Two of them are underground, in grottos that open with a Bomb or the Megaton Hammer. In the one east of the Castle Town drawbridge, by the moat, a Business Scrub sells you a Piece for 100 Rupees if you go as a child and know the password, which the Fairy Thought on the tree next to it tells you as an adult; the other is in a chest beneath a rock overhang in the west, near Gerudo Valley, and you have to open it as a child. Of the Skulltulas, the one in the lone pine in the east drops when you roll into the trunk, and the one in the stone circle grotto, by Lon Lon Ranch, needs the Boomerang or the Hookshot.

places.name: Lon Lon Ranch
places.intro: As a child you can get almost everything at Lon Lon Ranch: four Gold Skulltulas, a Piece of Heart and a Bottle, each marked on its map. Two of the Skulltulas only appear at night and need the Boomerang, in the house window and inside the stone tower at the back; the third, in the tree at the entrance, drops at any hour when you roll into the trunk, and the fourth appears as an adult in a crate in the grotto southeast of the ranch, if as a child you've read the Fairy Thought there and defeated the regular Skulltula. The Piece of Heart is at the back of the stone tower, behind some crates, and the Bottle is the prize of Talon's Super Cucco game, though you first have to wake him up at Hyrule Castle with the Cucco from the Weird Egg.

places.name: Hyrule Castle Town
places.intro: Three Pieces of Heart, two Bottles and a Gold Skulltula: that's what Hyrule Castle Town holds, with a child map and an adult map, because the town changes. Almost all of it is for child Link: two of the Pieces come at night, at the Treasure Chest Shop and by returning Richard, the lost puppy, to his owner, and the third is a prize at the Bombchu Bowling Alley, which doesn't open until you beat King Dodongo. The Skulltula is tucked inside a crate in the guard house at the entrance, and the Bottles are the remake's new one, a gift from the shopkeeper beside the road to the Temple of Time, and the Poe Collector's, as an adult, for five Big Poes.

places.name: Hyrule Castle
places.intro: Between the two Hyrule Castle maps, its grounds as a child and the outside of Ganon's Castle as an adult, there are three Gold Skulltulas and two Great Fairies. Two of the Skulltulas appear as a child, the one in the tree in the hedge garden and the one in the grotto that the Song of Storms opens by the tree at the moat, along with the Great Fairy of the spin attack, behind a boulder at the end of the dead-end path to the east. As an adult, what's left is the Skulltula on the ruined arch, which you only see if you turn around while crossing it, and the Great Fairy of Double Defense, covered by a pillar the Golden Gauntlets lift.

places.name: Kakariko Village
places.intro: Kakariko Village sits at the foot of Death Mountain, past the bridge from Hyrule Field, and it's one of the spots with the most collectibles on the map. Five of its six Gold Skulltulas appear as a child and at night, with the sword or the Slingshot, and the sixth, on the rock wall right next to the roof of Impa's House, as an adult, at night and with the Hookshot. The Pieces of Heart are split between the two ages, the Bottle comes from the Cucco Lady when you bring back her seven Cuccos, and the House of Skulltula has one more Piece waiting for you to gather 50 tokens.

places.name: Graveyard
places.intro: The Kakariko Graveyard has a map for each age, and between them they hold four Pieces of Heart, two Gold Skulltulas and a Magic Bean. As a child and at night, Dampé digs for 10 Rupees and every so often turns up a Piece, and the grave near the Royal Family's Tomb hides another in its crypt, which at that age only opens at night. As an adult come the race against Dampé's ghost, which gives the Piece on the second run (the first gives the Hookshot), and the ledge on the left wall, reached by the bean planted as a child. The Skulltulas appear at night on the wall at the entrance and, with Bugs, as a child and at any hour, in the soft soil beside Dampé's Grave.

places.name: Death Mountain Trail
places.intro: Along Death Mountain Trail, from Kakariko to the Crater, the map marks four Gold Skulltulas, a Piece of Heart, a Great Fairy and a Magic Bean. As a child, clear the boulder from Dodongo's Cavern with a Bomb or the Bomb Flower and make use of the soft soil left in front of it: Bugs for a Skulltula and a bean that serves as a shortcut when you're an adult. The Piece of Heart is on the ledge above the cavern entrance, and the Great Fairy of magic and Din's Fire is at the summit, behind the cracked wall next to Kaepora Gaebora. Of the other three Skulltulas, the one in the cracked wall by Kakariko appears at either age, and the two for adult Link at night are under boulders you have to break, one of them only with the Megaton Hammer.

places.name: Goron City
places.intro: Goron City, carved into Death Mountain, has only three collectibles on its map: two Gold Skulltulas and a Piece of Heart, split between the two ages. As a child, the Skulltula in the boulder maze on the upper floor is reached by blasting a path with Bombs, and the Piece comes out of the big spinning pot in the center: light its torches so it spins and drop a Bomb in from the plank on the floor above. As an adult, what's left is the other Skulltula, under a rocky ledge on the ceiling, which only the Hookshot can reach.

places.name: Death Mountain Crater
places.intro: Heat rules Death Mountain Crater, where the map marks three Pieces of Heart, two Gold Skulltulas, a Great Fairy and a Magic Bean. You enter from the mountain summit or from Goron City; as a child the heat puts you on a countdown, and as an adult, with the Goron Tunic, there's no rush. As a child you get the Skulltula in the crate at the summit entrance, the Piece the Business Scrub sells for 100 Rupees and the Skulltula in the soft soil of the Bolero of Fire, reached by playing that song: plant the bean there too. As an adult, that plant drops you on the dome-shaped rock with another Piece, the third, which you can also get as a child, is in a hollow in the wall as you climb down the nets from the entrance, and the Great Fairy who doubles your magic waits behind boulders only the Megaton Hammer can break.

places.name: Zora's River
places.intro: The Bean Seller is at the entrance to Zora's River, and upstream the map marks four Pieces of Heart and four Gold Skulltulas. As a child, get past the boulders at the entrance with a Bomb, buy every bean you can from him and plant one in the soft soil next to him. All four Pieces are for child Link: two on platforms you reach by gliding with a Cucco (or with the Boomerang, for the one at the waterfall) and two from the frogs on the stump, one for playing them their songs and winning their game and another for the Song of Storms. Of the Skulltulas, two are for child Link, the one in the Bean Seller's soft soil, with Bugs, and, at night, the one on the wall by the waterfall, and two for adult Link at night, high up on the walls and with the Hookshot.

places.name: Zora's Domain
places.intro: One per age: that's how the two collectibles in Zora's Domain are split, a Piece of Heart as a child and a Gold Skulltula as an adult, each in its spot on the map. For the Piece, light every torch on the lower floor with a Deku Stick, starting with the one at the foot of the stairs, and its chest will appear behind the waterfall. As an adult, with the domain frozen over, the Skulltula appears at night at the top of the frozen waterfall, and you bring it down with the Hookshot or an arrow.

places.name: Zora's Fountain
places.intro: Behind King Zora's throne, Zora's Fountain holds two Pieces of Heart, three Gold Skulltulas and a Great Fairy, with a map for each age. As a child it's Jabu-Jabu's pond, and as an adult, a frozen lake on the way to the Ice Cavern. The Great Fairy, the one with Farore's Wind, opens at either age, behind the cracked wall in the southeast corner, and two of the Skulltulas appear as a child: the one in the pine tree in that same corner and, at night and with the Boomerang, the one on the wall of the sunken arch. As an adult, one Piece waits on the farthest ice floe and another at the bottom, with the Zora Tunic and the Iron Boots, and the third Skulltula appears at night on the far side of a cave covered by two blocks with Zora markings, which the Silver Gauntlets lift.

places.name: Lake Hylia
places.intro: Lake Hylia is one of the fullest areas on the map: five Gold Skulltulas, three Pieces of Heart, a Bottle and a Magic Bean, across both ages. As a child, the soft soil right next to the laboratory gives a Skulltula with Bugs and a bean that lifts you to the roof as an adult, where one of the Pieces is; another comes from the owner of the Fishing Pond for a fish over 50 cm, and the third from the Lake Scientist, if you dive to the bottom of his pool with the Golden Scale. The Bottle with Ruto's Letter is at the bottom of the lake, by the tunnel to Zora's Domain, and needs the Silver Scale. Of the Skulltulas, three are for child Link and two for adult Link: the one in the crate at the bottom of the pool, with the Iron Boots, and the one in the crown of the big tree on the island, at night and with the Longshot.

places.name: Gerudo Valley
places.intro: To reach Gerudo's Fortress you have to cross Gerudo Valley, and its map marks four Gold Skulltulas, two Pieces of Heart and a Magic Bean. One of the Pieces is behind the big waterfall, which you reach by swimming, and the other, in a chest on a ledge in the canyon, is reached as a child by gliding with the Cucco by the bridge. On the cow's platform, at the foot of the waterfall, the soft soil gives a Skulltula with Bugs and a bean that also brings you close to the waterfall Piece as an adult. The other three Skulltulas appear at night: the one at the waterspout by the walkway, as a child and with the Boomerang, and the ones on the carpenters' tent and the rock arch across from it, as an adult and with the Hookshot.

places.name: Gerudo's Fortress
places.intro: Everything Gerudo's Fortress holds is for adult Link: two Pieces of Heart and two Gold Skulltulas, which the map places on the archery range and the rooftops. Rescuing the four carpenters earns you the Gerudo Token, which opens the horseback archery range: during the day, score 1,000 points on Epona to win a Piece, and come back at night with the Hookshot for the Skulltula on the far target. The high exit from the kitchen leads up to the rooftops, where the other Skulltula is at night and, on the highest rooftop, the chest with the second Piece, which you reach with the Longshot from the rock ledge above it.

places.name: Haunted Wasteland
places.intro: The Haunted Wasteland holds just one Gold Skulltula, as an adult, in the chamber beneath the stone monument on the way to the Desert Colossus. To cross it, get past the river of sand with the Hover Boots or the Longshot and follow the flags; at the monument, go in through the gap between the columns, climb down the ladder and knock the Skulltula down with your sword from the altar.

places.name: Desert Colossus
places.intro: With the Requiem of Spirit you reach the Desert Colossus as a child, and its map marks three Gold Skulltulas, a Piece of Heart, a Great Fairy and a Magic Bean. As an adult you get there by crossing the Haunted Wasteland. Go as a child to drop Bugs in the soft soil at the entrance to the Spirit Temple, which gives a Skulltula, and to plant the bean there: as an adult, its plant carries you over the top of the great rock, where another Skulltula sits at night, to the stone arch with the Piece of Heart. The third Skulltula appears at night high up on the rock wall to the right of the Spirit Temple, with the Hookshot, and the Great Fairy of Nayru's Love, behind the cracked wall north of the oasis, opens at both ages with a Bomb or a Bombchu.

places.name: Inside the Deku Tree
places.intro: Inside the Deku Tree is the game's first dungeon, entered as a child right as you leave Kokiri Forest with the sword and the shield. The map covers its five floors, from the top down to the second basement. Its four Gold Skulltulas fall to the sword or to the Slingshot you find inside, and in the remake all four can be collected on this first visit: the one in the back room of the basement no longer needs Bombs or the Boomerang, just burn the web with a Deku Stick. Queen Gohma, in the second basement, drops the Heart Container: stun her eye with the Slingshot and hit it with the sword.

places.name: Dodongo's Cavern
places.intro: Dodongo's Cavern is on the Death Mountain Trail and opens as a child by blowing up the boulder at the entrance with a Bomb Flower and the Goron's Bracelet. Its map has the cavern's two floors. Of its five Gold Skulltulas, four fall on the first visit, as a child; the one on the scarecrow's ledge means coming back as an adult with the Hookshot and the Scarecrow's Song, or with the Longshot. King Dodongo drops the Heart Container: a Bomb in the mouth and then the sword.

places.name: Inside Jabu-Jabu's Belly
places.intro: You enter Jabu-Jabu's Belly as a child from Zora's Fountain, by dropping a fish in front of Jabu-Jabu's mouth, and inside almost everything revolves around the Boomerang you get early on. The map has its three floors, basement included. The first Gold Skulltula falls to the sword in the water switch room; the other three, to the Boomerang, two of them together in the basement of the big room with the holes, aiming by hand because they can't be targeted. Barinade drops the Heart Container, also to Boomerang throws.

places.name: Forest Temple
places.intro: The Forest Temple is the first adult dungeon: you enter from the Sacred Forest Meadow with the Hookshot, and that same Hookshot knocks down its five Gold Skulltulas and pulls the tokens to you. The map has its five floors. It's best to grab them as you go, because each one falls in a room along the way: the entrance, the lobby, the two courtyards and the spinning room in the basement, right before the boss. The Heart Container is dropped by Phantom Ganon, with the Bow or the Hookshot at hand.

places.name: Fire Temple
places.intro: You reach the Fire Temple as an adult from Death Mountain Crater, wearing the Goron Tunic to withstand the heat. Its map has five floors, from 1F to 5F. Its five Gold Skulltulas ask for more than the sword: the Song of Time, Bombs, the Hookshot and, for two of them, the Scarecrow's Song you compose as a child and as an adult at Lake Hylia. The one behind the statue in the lobby and Volvagia's Heart Container both wait for the Megaton Hammer, so leave them for last.

places.name: Water Temple
places.intro: The Water Temple lies at the bottom of Lake Hylia and is entered as an adult with the Iron Boots and the Zora Tunic, changing the water level with Zelda's Lullaby. Its map has the four floors, from B1 to 3F. Of its five Gold Skulltulas, two can be collected before beating Dark Link, the one by the grate in the basement and the one behind the cracked underwater wall; the other three need the Longshot that fight leaves you, so the easy way is to get it first and then do a sweep of the central pillar, the whirlpool river and the waterfall with the boulders. Morpha drops the Heart Container at the end.

places.name: Shadow Temple
places.intro: The Shadow Temple, beneath the Kakariko Graveyard, opens as an adult with the Nocturne of Shadow and Din's Fire, and inside the Lenses of Truth and the Hover Boots are essential from the start. The map has its four basement floors. Its five Gold Skulltulas come up in the order of the route, in the room with the invisible scythes, in the one with the spikes on the ceiling, in the pit of the fan corridor, on the ledge in the boat room and inside the giant skulls; two fall to the Hookshot, the one in the boat room needs the Longshot and the Scarecrow's Song, and the one in the skulls, Bombs. The Heart Container is dropped by Bongo Bongo, with arrows or the Hookshot and the Lenses active.

places.name: Spirit Temple
places.intro: The Spirit Temple, at the Desert Colossus, is explored twice: first as a child, slipping through the small hole after talking to Nabooru, and then as an adult, pushing aside the big block in the lobby with the Silver Gauntlets. Its map has four floors, from 1F to 4F. Three of its five Gold Skulltulas can already be collected in the child section, two with the Boomerang or the Slingshot and one with the sword, and the other two, in the adult section, need the Song of Time and the Longshot with the Scarecrow's Song. For Twinrova's Heart Container you need the Mirror Shield, which you get in the temple itself.

places.name: Bottom of the Well
places.intro: You enter the Bottom of the Well as a child, once you drain the well in Kakariko Village by playing the Song of Storms in the Windmill. Inside, its two-floor map marks three Gold Skulltulas, and all of them need the Boomerang and the Lenses of Truth, which are earned in the basement. Without the Lenses you can't see the false walls, the invisible paths or the trapdoors; the three Skulltulas wait behind locked doors, two in the central area and one in the Like Like room.

places.name: Ice Cavern
places.intro: You enter the Ice Cavern as an adult from the frozen Zora's Fountain, following the ice floes to the cave at the back, and it's where you get the Iron Boots. Its map marks three Gold Skulltulas, and all three fall to the Hookshot. One is in the spinning blade room, among the stalagmites; for the other two, gather the Silver Rupees in that room to open the Dungeon Map room, fill a Bottle with Blue Fire there and use it to melt the two red ice walls in the blade room: behind them are the Compass room and the sliding ice block room.

places.name: Gerudo Training Ground
places.intro: The Gerudo Training Ground is the trial dungeon of Gerudo's Fortress, entered as an adult with the Gerudo Token. It holds no Gold Skulltulas or Pieces of Heart, so on this map it has no collectibles to check off; its reward is the Ice Arrows.

places.name: Ganon's Castle
places.intro: Ganon's Castle rises as an adult where Hyrule Castle used to stand, and it's the game's final dungeon. It holds no Gold Skulltulas or Pieces of Heart, so on this map it has no collectibles to check off. What there is outside, by the entrance path, is the Great Fairy of Double Defense and a Gold Skulltula on a ruined arch: those are on the Hyrule Castle map.

items.name: Behind the House of the Know-It-All Brothers
items.desc:
The House of the Know-It-All Brothers, on the hill across from the House of the Great Mido and next to the Forest Training Center, hides this Gold Skulltula on the back of its trunk. It only comes out at night, and only as a child.

Climb the hill and walk around the house to the back.

items.name: Bugs in the soft soil by the shop
items.desc:
Right behind the Kokiri Shop there is a patch of soft soil that hides a Gold Skulltula as a child, and all it takes to bring it out is a bottle of bugs.

As soon as you **empty the bottle of bugs onto the patch**, the Skulltula pops out of the ground: defeat it with your sword and grab the Gold Skulltula Token. It works at any time of day.

items.name: Back of the House of the Twins
items.desc:
This Gold Skulltula requires coming back to Kokiri Forest as an adult, at night, because it clings high up on the back of the House of the Twins, the one with the twin-peaked roof near the path to the Great Deku Tree's Meadow.

Your sword can't reach that high, but **the Hookshot takes it out from below**, and a second shot at the token brings it down to you.

items.name: Soft soil behind the shop
items.desc:
One of the Magic Beans you buy from the Bean Seller at Zora's River goes here, in the soft soil right beside the Kokiri Shop, and it's best to plant it as a child so it's ready when you come back.

As an adult, the plant's leaf **drops you on a small ledge with a ring of green Rupees** around a red one. The same patch also holds the bug Skulltula, so as a child you can do both things in one go.
items.hint: Plant it as a child and use it as an adult.

items.name: Saria's Song for the Skull Kid
items.desc:
As soon as you enter the Lost Woods from Kokiri Forest, the first path on the left leads to a Skull Kid playing his flute on a tall stump, who vanishes if you just walk up to him.

So **climb onto the low stump in front of him** and play Saria's Song on your Ocarina: the Skull Kid will become your friend and give you a Piece of Heart.

items.name: Memory game with the Ocarina
items.desc:
The Slingshot target area, the first path on the right as you come in from Kokiri Forest, hides a memory game with two Skull Kids. Go down the stairs ahead to the target tree and **pass to its right to climb onto the small stump**.

Then you have to repeat on your Ocarina what they play, in three rounds of five, six and eight notes. If you miss a note, the round starts over with a different melody, and the prizes scale up: Rupees in the first two and the Piece of Heart in the third.

items.name: Bugs in the soft soil by the bridge
items.desc:
Past the flute-playing Skull Kid, the first path on the left as you come in from Kokiri Forest, turn left again and you'll reach the area with the bridge to Hyrule Field. You'll recognize it by the Gossip Stone and the Business Scrub at the back who sells the bigger Deku Stick bag.

The soft soil is right by the path as you arrive: **pour a bottle of bugs onto it** and, when the Gold Skulltula surfaces, finish it off with your sword and grab the Gold Skulltula Token.

items.name: Bugs in the soft soil of the lone-tree clearing
items.desc:
To reach this patch, follow the Lost Woods route right, left, right, left and then, instead of heading for the Sacred Forest Meadow, turn left once more. It's the clearing with the lone tree, two Business Scrubs and a hole in the grass.

Once there, **drop the bugs on the soft soil to the right, next to one of the Scrubs**, and when the Gold Skulltula comes out, defeat it with your sword and grab the Gold Skulltula Token.

items.name: Ledge by the Forest Stage
items.desc:
Reaching the high ledge where this Gold Skulltula sits takes some groundwork as a child, because the only way up is the plant in the lone-tree clearing. To get to the clearing, turn right, left, right, left and left in the Lost Woods, then plant the bean in the soft soil on the right, next to a Business Scrub.

When you come back as an adult at night, **ride the plant up to the ledge** and defeat the Skulltula with your sword.

items.name: Soft soil by the bridge
items.desc:
Turning left twice from the Lost Woods entrance takes you to the area with the bridge to Hyrule Field, and its soft soil is a good place to plant a Magic Bean as a child.

When you return as an adult, **let the plant carry you up to the bridge** between Kokiri Forest and Hyrule Field and jump onto it: it's a handy shortcut during the trading sequence, when the Odd Mushroom expires after three minutes.
items.hint: Plant it as a child and use it as an adult.

items.name: Soft soil by the two Scrubs
items.desc:
Two Business Scrubs and a lone tree stand in the Lost Woods clearing you reach by turning right, left, right, left and left from the entrance, and there's a patch of soft soil there to plant a Magic Bean as a child. It's on the right, behind one of the Scrubs, and bugs will draw a Gold Skulltula out of it.

As an adult, **ride the plant up to the clearing's high ledge**, which holds another Gold Skulltula at night.
items.hint: Plant it as a child and use it as an adult.

items.name: Right-hand wall before the stairs
items.desc:
The maze of the Sacred Forest Meadow hides this Gold Skulltula, though it only appears as an adult. Make your way through while dodging the Moblins and, when you reach the midpoint, look at the wall on the right.

**Hit the Skulltula with the Hookshot** and fire it again to pull in the Gold Skulltula Token.

items.name: Business Scrub by the moat
items.desc:
Leave Hyrule Castle Town across the drawbridge and follow the wall east along the edge of the moat. Next to a tree you'll see a hole you can open with a Bomb or the Megaton Hammer: drop in and talk to the Business Scrub inside.

He only sells to those who know the password. To learn it, go to the tree next door as adult Link and read the Fairy Thought. Then come back as a child, talk to the Business Scrub and **choose "Sell somethin', will ya?"**: he'll offer you the Piece of Heart for 100 Rupees.

Buy it as a child, because as an adult he has already sold it to the Link of the past.
items.hint: It costs 100 Rupees.

items.name: Paradox of the chest from the past
items.desc:
At the western end of Hyrule Field, near the entrance to Gerudo Valley, the ground turns to reddish dirt. Head down the slope into a hollow beneath a rock overhang and look for the chest at the back.

It has to be as a child: as an adult the chest is already open and empty, and a Fairy Thought explains that it was never locked. **Open the chest as a child** and the Piece of Heart is yours.
items.hint: Read the Fairy Thought as an adult to learn why it's empty.

items.name: Lone pine in the east
items.desc:
In the east of Hyrule Field, between Zora's River and Kokiri Forest, a lone pine stands on top of a knoll next to a stream. A Gold Skulltula hides in it.

**Roll into the trunk** to knock it to the ground, finish it off with your sword and grab the Gold Skulltula Token.
items.hint: It's on top of a knoll, next to a stream.

items.name: Stone circle grotto by the ranch
items.desc:
In the grove southwest of Lon Lon Ranch, next to the exit toward Lake Hylia, a circle of stones on the ground covers a grotto. Open it with **a Bomb or a Megaton Hammer strike on the circle** and drop down the hole.

As soon as you enter, a Big Skulltula drops from the ceiling: defeat it with your sword. The gold one is on the wall; reach it with the Hookshot or the Boomerang, which also bring the Gold Skulltula Token to you.

items.name: Stone tower at the back
items.desc: At the back of Lon Lon Ranch, right behind the horse corral, there's a stone tower that serves as a silo. In one of its corners, some crates cover an opening: **push the crates aside and crawl through the opening** to the end, where the Piece of Heart awaits.

items.name: Tree on the way to the corral
items.desc: As soon as you enter Lon Lon Ranch, in the side yard to the left, there's a tree with a Gold Skulltula hidden in it: **roll into the trunk to knock it to the ground**, defeat it and grab the Gold Skulltula Token.

items.name: Crate in the grotto south of the ranch
items.desc:
For this Gold Skulltula to appear as an adult, child Link must read the Fairy Thought in the underground grotto southeast of Lon Lon Ranch, near the pond, and defeat the regular Skulltula.

Once that's done, come back as an adult. At the back, against the wall, there's a wooden crate. **Break it by rolling into it** and a Gold Skulltula will come out: defeat it with your sword and grab the Gold Skulltula Token. As a curiosity, the Fairy Thought will have changed.
items.hint: Kill the Skulltula in the past to find the gold one in the future.

items.name: Window of the house
items.desc:
If you look up at Talon's house at night, in Lon Lon Ranch next to the entrance arch, you'll see a Gold Skulltula in the upstairs window, too high for your sword.

**Throw the Boomerang at it from below**: it defeats it and brings you the Gold Skulltula Token in the same throw. During the day that wall is empty.

items.name: Inside the stone tower
items.desc:
The stone tower at the back of Lon Lon Ranch, behind the corral, holds a Gold Skulltula inside at night. Go in through the tower door and look up: it's high on the wall, above the clump of hay hanging below the window.

Only the Boomerang can reach it: **throw it from the tower floor** and it defeats the Skulltula and brings you the Gold Skulltula Token in the same throw. The Slingshot kills it, but the token stays up there.

items.name: Treasure Chest Shop
items.desc:
The Treasure Chest Shop is to the left of the Hyrule Castle Town square as you come in, down a side street. It only opens at night and charges 10 Rupees a game. The owner gives you a key: each of the five rooms has two chests and only one holds the key to the next; pick wrong and the game is over.

Equip the Lenses of Truth from the Equipment tab to see what's inside each chest. **Clear all five rooms and open the big chest in the prize room** to claim the Piece of Heart.
items.hint: Recommended: Lenses of Truth.

items.name: The lost puppy
items.desc:
Richard is the little white dog that runs around at night in one of the back alleys of Hyrule Castle Town, where a man is leaning out of the window of his house. Talk to Richard so he follows you.

With Richard at your heels, go to **the entrance to the square coming from Hyrule Field**. His owner will give you the Piece of Heart.
items.hint: She only gives the piece the first time; after that, Rupees.

items.name: Bombchu Bowling Alley
items.desc:
The Bombchu Bowling Alley is on the west side of the Market square in Hyrule Castle Town, and it doesn't open until you defeat King Dodongo.

Talk to the attendant: before you pay, she tells you which prize is up for grabs, and each game costs 10 Rupees. You have to clear three levels with 10 Bombchus, releasing them from behind the line so they reach the target at the back, with obstacles like a Cucco in the way.

The prize changes from one game to the next, so **keep playing until she announces the Piece of Heart** and win that game.
items.hint: 10 Rupees per game; the prize is announced before you pay.

items.name: Guard House
items.desc:
Next to the drawbridge, at the entrance to Hyrule Castle Town, is the guard house, a building full of pots with a Gold Skulltula hidden inside a wooden crate.

Go to the back wall and **roll into the crate farthest to the right**, the one to the right of the soldier as you face him.

items.name: Tree in the hedge garden
items.desc:
You can only explore the Hyrule Castle grounds as a child. Go up the path toward the castle and, to one side, step into the garden of hedges and flowers in front of you. Cross it westward to the far corner, by the castle wall, where there is a lone tree.

**Roll into the trunk** to knock the Gold Skulltula down; defeat it and collect the token.

items.name: Song of Storms grotto
items.desc:
To avoid the guard at the Hyrule Castle gate, climb the vines and drop into the moat by the entrance bridge. Swim east under the bridge and come out up the stone steps: right there, by the outer wall, is a tree with a circle of dirt at its base.

**Play the Song of Storms on that circle** to open a hole. The grotto has cracked walls you can blow open with Bombs: behind one of them is the Gold Skulltula. The Boomerang kills it and brings you the token.

items.name: Great Fairy: Spin Attack
items.desc:
At the east end of the Hyrule Castle grounds, hugging the right-hand wall, there is a dead-end path with a boulder at the end. To keep the guard from stopping you, climb the vines on the wall.

At the end of the path, **blow up the boulder with a Bomb and crawl through the gap** to the Great Fairy's Fountain. Play Zelda's Lullaby on the Triforce emblem and accept the 50-Rupee offering: the Great Fairy will enhance your Spin Attack with a magical shock wave.
items.hint: She asks for a 50-Rupee offering and enhances the Spin Attack with a shock wave.

items.name: Small roof behind Impa's House
items.desc:
The piece sits in plain sight on a small red-tiled roof behind Impa's House, up against the mountain. From the blue roof of the house, **drop down onto the small roof behind it** and pick it up. From there you can get down to the cow's stable.

As a child, talk to Kaepora Gaebora at the top of Death Mountain and the owl will drop you on Impa's roof. As an adult you need the Hookshot.
items.hint: As an adult, Hookshot from the roof of the House of Skulltula.

items.name: Windmill
items.desc:
Inside the Windmill, at the back of the village, the piece waits up top, on a piece of furniture on the upper walkway.

As an adult you get there through Dampé's Grave, in the Graveyard. When his race is over, the exit stairs are broken: **fire the Hookshot at the target above the door** and follow the corridor. You come out at the top of the Windmill, next to the spinning platform; climb onto the furniture against the wall and grab the piece.
items.hint: As an adult you get in through Dampé's Grave.

items.name: The man on the roof
items.desc:
The man on the roof is sitting on top of **the Potion Shop, next to the watchtower and across from the Windmill**, and all you have to do is reach him and talk to him to get the Piece of Heart.

As an adult, the Hookshot is enough: stand on the railing across from the Windmill and hook onto the roof.
items.hint: As an adult you need the Hookshot.

items.name: House under construction
items.desc:
While the carpenters are building the house under construction, as a child and at night, the Gold Skulltula hangs on the brick wall of the site, above the ground. **Go up the plank ramp to the scaffolding walkway** and you'll have it right in front of you, on the wall.

Your sword is enough to kill it, so you don't need anything else to claim the token.

items.name: Tree at the entrance
items.desc: The big pine tree near the entrance from Hyrule Field, in the lower part of the village, hides a Gold Skulltula at night that drops to the ground as a child if you **roll into the pine's trunk**. Once it's down, finish it off and collect the token.

items.name: Watchtower
items.desc:
Halfway up the ladder of the watchtower, in the center of the village, a Gold Skulltula hangs at night that you attack from the bottom: **shoot it with the Slingshot or send a Bombchu up the ladder**.

When it dies, climb the ladder: the token stays on it, halfway up, and you can grab it without going all the way to the top.
items.hint: Get rid of it before climbing the tower toward the man on the roof.

items.name: House by the mountain gate
items.desc: On your way up to the Death Mountain gate, in the upper part of the village, you'll see a house right next to it, past the watchtower. As a child and at night, **go around it along the grassy path at the back** and check its walls until you find the Gold Skulltula. It's at ground level, so you can take it down with your sword and claim the token without needing any items.

items.name: House of Skulltula
items.desc:
The House of Skulltula, home of the cursed family, is the first one on the right as you come in from Hyrule Field, and it has cobwebs over the door. As a child and at night, the Gold Skulltula appears on **the front of the house, to the left of the entrance steps**, at ground level; during the day you can already see its web there.

If it's daytime, play the Sun's Song to bring on the night. Your sword takes care of it in no time, and then all that's left is to collect the token.

items.name: Above Impa's House
items.desc:
You have to come back as an adult and at night for this Gold Skulltula, which is on the rock wall right next to the blue roof of Impa's House, the big house on the southern edge of the village. You need the Hookshot.

Go around the house on one side to the rock wall behind it, which has vines, and **climb them up to the blue roof**. From up there you'll see the Skulltula on the rock, next to the roof: take it down with the Hookshot, which also brings you the token.

items.name: Gravedigging tour with Dampé
items.desc:
As a child and at night, Dampé, the gravekeeper, offers his "Heart-Pounding Gravedigging Tour" in the Graveyard. If you arrive during the day, play the Sun's Song there: night falls and Dampé comes out right away. Accept and stay in the central plaza, because if you wander off the tour ends.

Stand next to one of the dirt mounds and **ask him to dig: each attempt costs 10 Rupees**. Sometimes he hits something hard and asks for 5 more to keep going, and either a rock or the piece can come up, at random. Keep at it until it appears. The location is completely random.
items.hint: 10 Rupees per mound; sometimes he asks for 5 more to keep digging.

items.name: Race against Dampé
items.desc:
Dampé's Grave is the headstone with flowers that has smoke coming out of it, in the fenced area on the left, up a few steps. As an adult and at night, **pull on it to open the hole and go down into the catacombs**. Down there, follow his ghost to the end without losing sight of him; the first race gives you the Hookshot.

The Piece of Heart comes with the second. Leave with the Hookshot through the target above the broken stairs (you'll come out in the Kakariko Windmill), go back to the Graveyard, go down the hole again, which stays open, and reach the finish in one minute or less.
items.hint: The first race gives you the Hookshot; the piece comes with the second.

items.name: Grave near the Royal Family's Tomb
items.desc:
Near the Royal Family's Tomb, in the upper part of the Graveyard: stand with your back to the tomb, facing the exit, and among the headstones on your left it's **the first one starting from the left**. As an adult it always opens; as a child, only at night (during the day the boy who watches over the graves stops you; the Sun's Song saves you the wait).

Pull on the headstone and go down the hole: the chest with the Piece of Heart is at the back of the crypt, with no enemies guarding it.
items.hint: As a child the grave only opens at night.

items.name: Ledge on the wall
items.desc:
High up on the left wall of the Graveyard, above Dampé's Grave and the soft soil, there is a ledge with the Piece of Heart in plain sight on a stone pillar, and you can't reach it from below without help.

If you plant a Magic Bean in that soft soil as a child, when you come back as an adult **climb onto the leaf and let it carry you up to the ledge**. Once up there, grab the piece from the pillar.
items.hint: The piece sits in plain sight on a pillar on the wall.

items.name: Graveyard wall
items.desc:
At night, in the narrow alley between Dampé's Hut and the stone wall with the iron fence, by the Graveyard entrance, a Gold Skulltula comes out high up. During the day you'll see a golden web in that spot marking where it will appear.

**Defeat it with the Hookshot or the Boomerang and bring the token back with it.**

items.name: Bugs in the soft soil
items.desc: With a bottle of Bugs and as a child, at any time of day, go to the soft soil patch in the left-hand corner of the Graveyard, at the back, by the wall and near Dampé's Grave, and **release them on it so a Gold Skulltula comes out**. Kill it as soon as it pops up and collect the token.
items.hint: It's the same patch where you plant the Magic Bean.

items.name: Graveyard soft soil
items.desc: Beneath the high ledge on the left wall of the Graveyard, next to Dampé's Grave, is the soft soil where we recommend you **plant a Magic Bean as a child**. When you come back as an adult, the leaf carries you up to the ledge that holds the Piece of Heart.
items.hint: Plant it as a child and use it as an adult.

items.name: Ledge above Dodongo's Cavern
items.desc:
Above the entrance to Dodongo's Cavern is the ledge with this Piece of Heart, in plain sight in a nook in the rock. You need to plant a Magic Bean in the soft soil as a child.

As an adult, ride the bean plant and hop off when it passes by the ledge to grab the Piece of Heart.

items.name: Bugs in the soft soil by the cavern
items.desc:
The soft soil for this Gold Skulltula is in front of Dodongo's Cavern.

With the entrance cleared, **drop the bugs from the bottle onto the soft soil** and, as soon as the Gold Skulltula pops out, defeat it with your sword and collect the token.
items.hint: You can plant a Magic Bean in the same patch.

items.name: Cracked wall near Kakariko
items.desc:
Leaving Kakariko Village toward the mountain, before you reach Dodongo's Cavern, there's a wall of cracked rocks on the right side of the trail that doesn't match the rest: you can hear the Skulltula behind it.

**Open the wall with a Bomb or, as an adult, with the Megaton Hammer**, step into the alcove and defeat the Gold Skulltula, which sits on the back wall at sword height.

items.name: Above Dodongo's Cavern
items.desc:
The railed ledge from which, as a child, you drop the Bomb Flower onto Dodongo's Cavern, next to the turnoff to Goron City, has a few rocks against the wall. This Gold Skulltula appears under them when you come back as an adult, at night.

**Break the rocks with the Megaton Hammer or a Bomb**, the only things that can destroy them, then defeat the Skulltula and collect its token.

items.name: Falling-rocks path
items.desc:
Past Dodongo's Cavern, the trail climbs to the stretch where volcanic rocks rain down and ends at the net wall that leads to the summit. This Gold Skulltula appears at the foot of that wall, as an adult and at night.

Facing the wall, on the right as you climb, next to the rock arch, there's a pile of rocks that Bombs can't break: **hit it with the Megaton Hammer** and, with the rocks in pieces, finish off the Skulltula and collect the token.

items.name: Soft soil at Dodongo's Cavern
items.desc:
Before planting a Magic Bean here, as a child you have to remove the boulder blocking Dodongo's Cavern, using the Bomb Flower above and the Goron's Bracelet. Then plant it in the soft soil in front of the entrance.

As an adult, the plant passes over the Piece of Heart ledge and carries you up to the falling-rocks stretch: **a shortcut that skips the boulder blocking the trail**.
items.hint: Plant it as a child and use it as an adult.

items.name: Great Fairy: magic
items.desc:
At the very top, on the summit of Death Mountain, Kaepora Gaebora waits perched near the entrance to the Crater. **The wall of cracked rocks to his left can be brought down with a Bomb** or, as an adult, with the Megaton Hammer, and the fountain is behind it.

Inside, play Zelda's Lullaby on the Triforce emblem. The Great Fairy will ask you for an offering of 25 Rupees: accept, and she'll give you the Magic Meter and Din's Fire. If you climb up as a child, bring the Hylian Shield for the falling-rocks stretch.
items.hint: She asks for an offering of 25 Rupees. Reward: Magic Meter and Din's Fire.

items.name: Spinning pot
items.desc:
The big pot with faces in the middle of Goron City's bottom floor only starts spinning when, as a child, **you light the torches around it**. Din's Fire works, or a lit Deku Stick, lit for example in Darunia's room, which opens when you play Zelda's Lullaby at its door. They stay lit even if you come back later.

Then go up to the floor above, walk out onto the wooden plank that juts out over the pot and drop a Bomb into its top, or throw a Bomb Flower at it with the Goron's Bracelet. It'll drop the piece on the floor along with 10 Rupees.
items.hint: If it lands on another face, it gives other prizes: try again until you get it.

items.name: Boulder maze
items.desc:
The boulder maze room is on Goron City's top floor, the one with the entrance from Death Mountain Trail, and as a child you cross it by blasting a path through the blocks with Bombs.

At the far end, next to two chests, there's a wooden crate with the Gold Skulltula inside: **roll into the crate to break it**, defeat the Skulltula with your sword and collect the token.

items.name: Rock overhang on the ceiling
items.desc:
As an adult, in Goron City, one floor above the lowest level, go around the platform counterclockwise. Before entering the tunnel, look up: the Gold Skulltula is on the underside of the rock overhang on the ceiling.

**Knock it down with the Hookshot**, which brings you the token while it's at it.

items.name: Hole in the Crater wall
items.desc:
Entering the Crater from the summit of Death Mountain, the entrance ledge overlooks a great wall that drops down toward the Bolero of Fire platform. Some climbing nets hang from the edge of that ledge: **climb down them** and, a little lower, you'll find the piece in a hole in the wall, between two nets.

As a child, the heat will burn you up quickly. As an adult, with the Goron Tunic there's no rush.
items.hint: As a child there's a heat timer: be quick.

items.name: Domed rock in the Crater
items.desc:
As a child, **play the Bolero of Fire on the ocarina** and, once in the Crater, plant a bean in the soft soil next to the platform.

Come back as an adult wearing the Goron Tunic, **ride the leaf and hop off when it passes over one of the tall rocks**: the piece is waiting up top.
items.hint: You need to learn the Bolero of Fire.

items.name: Crate at the summit entrance
items.desc:
If you enter the Crater as a child from the summit of Death Mountain, rather than from Goron City, a few steps from the entrance, on the left, you'll see two wooden crates against the rock wall, next to a pot. The Gold Skulltula is inside the one next to the pot.

**Break the crates by rolling into them**, defeat the Skulltula and collect the token.
items.hint: Use Nayru's Love if you can't take the heat.

items.name: Bugs in the soft soil by the Bolero platform
items.desc:
This Gold Skulltula forces you to travel through time, because it only comes out as a child and the Bolero of Fire is learned as an adult. As a child, playing that song is the only way to reach its soft soil, a few steps from the Bolero platform.

You appear on the platform: **release the bugs in the soft soil beside it**, defeat the Skulltula and collect the token without dawdling, because the heat keeps draining your hearts.
items.hint: As a child the heat drains your hearts bit by bit: don't dawdle.

items.name: Soft soil in the Crater
items.desc:
Next to the Bolero of Fire platform, in the central area of the Crater, there's a soft soil patch that as a child you can only reach by playing that song. **Plant the Magic Bean and leave right away**, with another warp song for example, because the heat puts you on a timer.

When you come back as an adult, the plant passes over the domed rock of one Piece of Heart and then by the climbable wall of the other. It also carries you up to the summit entrance area.
items.hint: Plant it as a child and use it as an adult.

items.name: Great Fairy: double magic
items.desc:
From Darunia's room in Goron City, as an adult you go down to the lower part of the Crater. If you've just beaten Volvagia, the blue warp leaves you on the central platform: cross the chain bridge to the west and keep going along that shore. Two piles of rocks block a passage in the wall: **knock them down with the Megaton Hammer**.

In the fountain, step onto the emblem and play Zelda's Lullaby. The Great Fairy of Wisdom will ask you for an offering of 200 Rupees for the fountain: accept, and she'll double your Magic Meter.
items.hint: She asks for an offering of 200 Rupees. Reward: doubles your Magic Meter.

items.name: Pillar in the middle of the river
items.desc:
The piece is on a tall platform surrounded by water, in the middle of Zora's River, and as a child you reach it by gliding with a Cucco from the wooded area next to it. You climb up to that area by vines, without a Cucco in your arms, but up top, among the ferns on the left, a hole leads to a grotto with a chest and a Cucco. **Leave the grotto through the flower with the Cucco in your arms, run to the edge and jump to glide over to the platform.**

As an adult you get there by riding the bean plant or with the Hover Boots.
items.hint: As an adult, with the planted bean or the Hover Boots.

items.name: Ledge by the waterfall
items.desc:
At the end of Zora's River, beside the waterfall that hides the entrance to Zora's Domain, there's a free-standing platform with the piece.

Grab the Cucco at the start of the river, next to the Bean Seller, and carry it upriver with you. Once by the waterfall, climb to the highest point, **jump with it and glide to the platform**.
items.hint: As an adult you can only reach it with the Hover Boots.

items.name: Frog game
items.desc:
The frogs for this piece, the Fabulous Five Froggish Tenors, sit on stumps in the pond of a grotto cut into the rock, halfway along Zora's River. Go as a child, talk to them and they'll ask you to play them something on the ocarina. They give you Rupees for each new song:
- Zelda's Lullaby
- Epona's Song
- Saria's Song
- Sun's Song
- Song of Time

Once you've played them all, they propose their game: a bug appears above a frog and **you quickly play its note so it jumps up to eat it**. Get the whole sequence right and the piece is yours; if you miss, you can try again.
items.hint: Memorize which note each frog plays.

items.name: The frogs in the rain
items.desc: Halfway along Zora's River, you'll find a stump with five frogs in a cave. You have to play the **Song of Storms** on the ocarina. After you play it, the frogs will reward you with a Piece of Heart.

items.name: Bugs in the soft soil by the Bean Seller
items.desc:
Next to the Bean Seller, at the start of Zora's River, there's a soft soil patch hiding a Gold Skulltula, and you need a bottle of bugs to bring it out.

**Empty the bottle of bugs onto the soft soil**: the Skulltula will poke out of the ground. Defeat it with your sword and collect the token.

items.name: Wall by the waterfall
items.desc:
At the end of Zora's River, by the waterfall, this Gold Skulltula only comes out at night, as a child.

From the grassy ledge next to the waterfall, climb down the rock to the shore below, by the water.

The Skulltula is on the wall of the low rock on that shore. Get close and attack with your sword.

items.name: Above the raised grottos
items.desc:
High up on the rock wall above the plateau with the grottos, in the middle of Zora's River, a Gold Skulltula comes out at night, and the Hookshot only reaches it if you climb onto the plateau itself.

As an adult, you climb up the wall of vines between the rocks, next to the water. Up top, walk to the edge and **fire the Hookshot at the top of the wall** to defeat it and bring back the token.
items.hint: From the path below you'd need the Longshot.

items.name: Above the bridge
items.desc:
Above the last bridge on Zora's River, in the cave leading to the Zora's Domain waterfall, there's a very tall rock wall where a Gold Skulltula settles at night.

**Hit it with the Hookshot from the bridge itself** and collect the token.

items.name: Soft soil by the Bean Seller
items.desc:
Right as you enter Zora's River, two cracked boulders block the way; blow them up with a Bomb.

Just behind them, sitting next to a fence, is the Bean Seller, and as a child it's worth buying a few from him: the first costs 10 Rupees and each one after goes up by 10. **Plant one in the soft soil beside him**, using it from your inventory.
items.hint: Plant it as a child and use it as an adult.

items.name: Frozen waterfall
items.desc:
As an adult, with Zora's Domain frozen over, the Gold Skulltula comes out at night at the top of the frozen waterfall, where the diving game was as a child. You get there through the corridor on King Zora's floor, which opens onto a high gallery.

Look over the edge and to your left: it's on a column covered in frozen plants, up against the wall. **Reach it with the Hookshot or knock it down with an arrow** to claim the token.

items.name: Farthest ice floe
items.desc:
The piece sits on top of the farthest ice floe in the frozen Zora's Fountain, away from the path to the Ice Cavern. As an adult, you enter the fountain through the passage behind the frozen King Zora's throne.

**Jump from block to block all the way to the last one**: they're slippery ice blocks, so judge each jump carefully. If you fall in the water, swim back to the start and climb up again.

items.name: Bottom of the fountain
items.desc:
This Piece of Heart waits at the bottom of Zora's Fountain, among a pile of Green Rupees. As an adult you need two things: the Zora Tunic, which King Zora gives you when you free him, to breathe underwater, and the Iron Boots, to sink.

With the Zora Tunic on, get into the water, **put on the Iron Boots and sink to the bottom**, grab the piece, and take the boots off to float back up.

items.name: Wall above the sunken arch
items.desc: As soon as you enter Zora's Fountain from Zora's Domain, follow the shore to a ruined stone arch, half sunk in the water and set against the rock wall with vines. Climb to the top of the arch: at night, a Gold Skulltula appears on that wall, and as a child you can reach it with the Boomerang.
items.hint: You get the Boomerang inside Jabu-Jabu's Belly.

items.name: Pine tree in the southeast corner
items.desc:
In the southeast corner of Zora's Fountain, the one with the pine trees at the foot of the cliff, next to the wall that hides the Great Fairy's Fountain, there is a tree that hides a Gold Skulltula as a child, at any time of day.

No swimming needed: from the offering bowl in front of Lord Jabu-Jabu, go down to the right and follow the dirt path along the shore. **Roll into the pine tree** to knock the Skulltula down, defeat it with your sword, and grab the token.

items.name: Cave behind the Zora-marked blocks
items.desc:
As an adult, go to the far southeast end of Zora's Fountain, where two black stone blocks with Zora markings cover the entrance to a cave. **Lift them with the Silver Gauntlets** and go in.

Inside, invisible Skulltulas hang from the ceiling; dodge them, or see them with the Lenses of Truth. At the back, climb the vines and come out onto an outdoor ledge.

The Gold Skulltula only **comes out at night**. It appears above the mouth of a cave on the ledge, and you can knock it down with the Hookshot and collect the token.
items.hint: Inside, four invisible Skulltulas hang from the ceiling.

items.name: Great Fairy: Farore's Wind
items.desc:
From the offering bowl in front of Lord Jabu-Jabu, follow the ruined shore on the right on foot to the southeast corner, the one with the trees at the foot of the cliff. There, the Great Fairy's Fountain hides behind a cracked section of the rock wall.

**Set a Bomb or a Bombchu next to the cracked wall** to open the way. Inside, play Zelda's Lullaby while standing on the Triforce emblem on the floor. Before giving you Farore's Wind, the Great Fairy asks for an offering of 100 Rupees, which get thrown into the fountain, so bring them with you.
items.hint: She asks for an offering of 100 Rupees: bring them with you.

items.name: Diving in the laboratory
items.desc:
Inside the Lakeside Laboratory, the building on the shore, there is a deep pool, and the Piece of Heart is the reward for diving down and touching its bottom, which you can only manage with the Golden Scale, the prize from the Fishing Pond.

It doesn't matter whether you go as a child or as an adult: jump into the water, **dive down until you touch the bottom of the pool**, and when you climb out, the scientist will give you the piece.
items.hint: The Golden Scale is the fishing prize as an adult.

items.name: Laboratory roof
items.desc:
As a child, plant a Magic Bean in the soft soil next to the Lakeside Laboratory at Lake Hylia, and come back as an adult. Ride the leaf: it loops over the lake and drops you on the wooden balcony of the laboratory tower.

**Climb the ladder to the lookout at the top**, where the Piece of Heart is.
items.hint: Watch out for the crows on the roof: they can knock you down.

items.name: Fishing as a child
items.desc:
The Fishing Pond is on a small island in Lake Hylia, and its owner lends you the rod for 10 Rupees. When you catch a fish, keep it, and when you're done, talk to the owner and tell him you're quitting: he'll measure your best catch and, **if it's over 50 cm, as a child he gives you the Piece of Heart**.

The **biggest fish** are usually found **in the center of the pond**.
items.hint: Each attempt costs 10 Rupees; the prize is for a fish over 50 cm.

items.name: Bugs in the soft soil by the laboratory
items.desc: Up against the wall of the Lakeside Laboratory, next to some barrels and sacks, there is a patch of soft soil. As a child, at any time of day, the Gold Skulltula comes out as soon as you **open a bottle of Bugs over the patch of soil**: the bugs crawl into the hole and it climbs out of the ground. Your sword is enough to defeat it and keep the token.

items.name: Laboratory wall
items.desc:
A bridge leads out from behind the Lakeside Laboratory. As a child, at night, as soon as you step onto it, look to the right: on the round tower of the building, next to a pipe, is this Gold Skulltula, too high for your sword.

**From the bridge itself, throw the Boomerang at it**: it knocks it down and brings you the token.

items.name: Cave on the west shore
items.desc:
As a child, follow the west shore of Lake Hylia south all the way to the end, where a nook in the rock holds some pots, a barrel, and a Fairy Thought on the wall. From there, get into the water and swim to the shore next to it: in the rock wall you'll see a low gap with a stone lintel.

**Crawl through that gap** and you'll come to a small, dark cave. The Gold Skulltula is on the wall opposite; defeat it with your sword and collect the token.
items.hint: Crawl through the hole to find the Gold Skulltula.

items.name: Crate at the bottom of the laboratory pool
items.desc:
The pool in the Lakeside Laboratory hides a wooden crate at the bottom with a Gold Skulltula inside. To reach it as an adult, put on the Iron Boots and drop into the water.

Once down there, **roll into the crate to break it**, finish off the Skulltula, and collect the token with the Hookshot.

items.name: Tree on the big island
items.desc:
On the biggest island in the lake, the one with the Serenade of Water platform, there is a huge tree with a hollow crown. As an adult, **aim the Longshot at the top of the tree to pull yourself up** to the crown; the Hookshot won't reach.

The Gold Skulltula only comes out at night, inside the crown: if it's daytime, play the Sun's Song right there and it will appear. Defeat it with your sword and collect the token.

items.name: Soft soil by the laboratory
items.desc:
As a child, plant a Magic Bean in the patch of soft soil up against the wall of the Lakeside Laboratory, the same one as the Bugs Skulltula. When you come back as an adult, a plant shaped like a ring of colorful leaves will have sprouted.

**Climb onto the leaves and they'll fly you** around the lake to the laboratory roof.
items.hint: Plant it as a child and use it as an adult.

items.name: Behind the waterfall
items.desc:
Behind the big waterfall in Gerudo Valley, on the riverbank at the bottom of the canyon, there is a small chamber carved into the rock, above the water. To get there, go down to the cow's corner at the foot of the waterfall, gliding with the Cucco or jumping into the river and swimming out.

From there, follow the bank toward the waterfall, pass the Gossip Stone, and jump across the wet rocks behind the falling water. Then **climb the steps carved into the rock** up to the chamber, where the Piece of Heart is waiting.
items.hint: If the current carries you off, you end up in Lake Hylia.

items.name: Chest on the canyon ledge
items.desc:
In Gerudo Valley, past the bridge, on the carpenters' tent side, go to the edge of the canyon next to the piles of dark rocks by the rock arch. Below, halfway down to the river, there is a narrow ledge with a chest.

If you're a child, **use the Cucco to glide** down to the chest.

If you're an adult, **drop from the edge onto the ledge** and open the chest.

To get back, follow the ledge and jump into the river: the current carries you to Lake Hylia.
items.hint: The chest is on the cliff face.

items.name: Waterspout by the footbridge
items.desc:
When you enter Gerudo Valley from Hyrule Field, the first thing you come to is a small wooden footbridge over a pool. At night, the Gold Skulltula is under the planks, on the brick wall next to the spout of water falling into the pool.

Drop into the water from one side of the footbridge, climb out onto the stone bank below, and **throw the Boomerang at it** to knock it down and bring back the token. Then climb back up to the footbridge.

items.name: Bugs in the soft soil by the cow
items.desc:
At the foot of the big waterfall, on the upper stretch of the river, there is a corner with a cow, a Gerudo, and a patch of soft soil. As a child, you get there by gliding with the Cucco at the edge of the cliff, to the left of the big bridge (you can stop on a ledge and jump again), or by jumping into the river and swimming out.

Once there, **release the Bugs from the bottle onto the soft soil** and defeat the Gold Skulltula that comes out to collect the token.

items.name: Behind the tent
items.desc:
Past the bridge, on the side of the valley facing Gerudo's Fortress, is the carpenters' tent. To cross as an adult, jumping the broken bridge with Epona is enough; the Longshot or the repaired bridge, if you rescued the carpenters, also work.

At night, go around the tent to the ruins behind it. The Gold Skulltula climbs the carved stone wall, halfway up: **knock it down with the Hookshot, which brings you the token while it's at it**.

items.name: Rock arch across from the tent
items.desc:
On the path from the carpenters' tent to Gerudo's Fortress, there is a big natural arch of reddish rock, with two piles of dark rocks at its foot. At night, a Gold Skulltula climbs the inner face of the arch.

Stand between the piles of rocks, look up at the top of the arch until you spot it, and **shoot the Hookshot at it to knock it down**: when you kill it, the Hookshot itself brings the token to you.

items.name: Soft soil in the Gerudo canyon
items.desc:
This soft soil shares its spot with the cow and the Gerudo, at the foot of the big waterfall, and it's also the patch for the Bugs Gold Skulltula. As a child, glide down with the Cucco from the big bridge or swim out of the river, and plant the Magic Bean.

As an adult, the leaf goes down and up the waterfalls, passing two Red Rupees, and **halfway up the big waterfall, jump through the water** into the Piece of Heart's nook.
items.hint: Plant it as a child and use it as an adult.

items.name: Horseback archery - 1,000 points
items.desc:
The Gerudo Token you get for rescuing the four carpenters opens up the horseback archery range. Go during the day, because at night the woman in charge won't let you play, and bring Epona. Each run costs 30 Rupees.

Epona runs the course on her own and you have 20 arrows for the targets and the pots; each pot or bull's-eye is worth 100 points. **Reach 1,000 points to win the Piece of Heart**; with 1,400, you also take home the Biggest Quiver.
items.hint: Each game costs 30 Rupees; with 1,400 points, the Biggest Quiver.

items.name: Archery range target
items.desc:
With the Gerudo Token you can enter the horseback archery range, and at night there is a Gold Skulltula on the big round target on a post at the end of the course. Ride or walk the whole course, with Epona or on foot, to the circular area at the far end.

**Shoot the Hookshot at it once you have a clear shot** to kill the Skulltula and bring back the token; if you can't see it from the front, go around the target.

items.name: Upper rooftop
items.desc:
At night, the Gold Skulltula appears on the side rooftops of Gerudo's Fortress, a few steps from the Piece of Heart chest: it's on the brick wall of the block that rises next to the cliff rock.

To get up there, as an adult, go in through the door to the kitchen corridor, cross it without being seen, and use the high exit at the back, which leads out onto the rooftops. Stand in front of that wall and **shoot the Hookshot at it**, or jump at it with your sword, to collect the token.

items.name: Inside the monument
items.desc:
To reach the stone monument in the Haunted Wasteland, cross the river of sand as an adult, following the flags. At the monument, go in through the gap between the columns and climb down the ladder to the room below.

The Gold Skulltula is on the back wall, above the altar: **climb onto the altar and knock it down with your sword**. If you light the torches with Fire Arrows or Din's Fire, a chest with a Business Scrub Seed appears.

items.name: Stone arch by the temple
items.desc:
Near the entrance to the Spirit Temple there is a stone arch that only the magic plant can reach, so the job starts as a child. Travel to the Desert Colossus with the Requiem of Spirit and plant a Magic Bean in the soft soil to the left of the temple entrance.

The leaf ride, as an adult, passes over two rock platforms and ends above the arch: **when you're over it, jump off and grab the Piece of Heart**.

items.name: Bugs in the soft soil by the temple
items.desc:
As a child, play the Requiem of Spirit to travel to the Desert Colossus and walk from the arrival platform to the steps of the Spirit Temple: the patch of soft soil is just to the left of the entrance, up against the rock wall.

In that patch, which is also where you plant the Magic Bean, **release the Bugs from a bottle** and the Gold Skulltula will come out right away: defeat it with your sword and collect the token.

items.name: Top of the big rock
items.desc:
A big rock rises near the Great Fairy's Fountain, and its top, with a crater-shaped hollow, is the second platform the Magic Bean plant from the Spirit Temple's soft soil passes over. As an adult, ride the leaf and, when it reaches that rock, **jump onto the top and drop into the hollow**.

The Gold Skulltula only comes out there at night: if it's daytime, play the Sun's Song and it will appear. Kill it with your sword and grab the Gold Skulltula Token.

items.name: Rock wall beside the temple
items.desc:
At night, this Desert Colossus Gold Skulltula appears high up on the rock wall to the right of the Spirit Temple.

Find the Skulltula and **hit it with the Hookshot** to kill it and pull in the Gold Skulltula Token.

items.name: Soft soil by the temple
items.desc:
You have to come here as a child with the Requiem of Spirit to plant the Magic Bean: the soft soil is to the left of the Spirit Temple entrance, and dropping Bugs on it also brings out a Gold Skulltula.

As an adult, the plant **carries you over two rock platforms to the stone arch** with the Piece of Heart, and the second platform holds the other Gold Skulltula, which only comes out at night.
items.hint: Plant it as a child, use it as an adult.

items.name: Great Fairy: Nayru's Love
items.desc:
North of the oasis, across the pond if you're looking from the Spirit Temple, a cracked rock wall between the palm trees hides the Great Fairy's Fountain. You can open it just the same as a child, arriving with the Requiem of Spirit, or as an adult, crossing the Haunted Wasteland.

**Blow up the cracked rock with a Bomb, a Bombchu or the Megaton Hammer**, go in, stand on the Triforce emblem and play Zelda's Lullaby. The Great Fairy will ask you for an offering of 300 Rupees for the fountain: accept, and she'll give you Nayru's Love.
items.hint: She asks for an offering of 300 Rupees.

items.name: Compass room
items.desc:
The Compass room, on the top floor of the Deku Tree, keeps this Gold Skulltula in an out-of-the-way corner. Step on the switch to raise the platforms and, instead of going for the Compass, jump into the side alcove on the left.

**On the back wall, behind the small chest**, it's within easy reach: kill it with your sword and grab the Gold Skulltula Token.

items.name: Basement vines
items.desc:
When you drop onto the big web in the middle of the main room, you'll break through it and land in the water of the basement. In the round pool on the right, this Gold Skulltula waits on the wall of vines that climbs back up to the main room.

You have to attack it from a distance, so **knock it down with the Slingshot or the Boomerang** from the water, then climb the vines up to the Gold Skulltula Token.
items.hint: You get the Slingshot in this very dungeon.

items.name: Basement gate
items.desc:
On the first basement floor of the Deku Tree there's a water channel that ends in a barred gate, and this Gold Skulltula clings to it.

Climb onto the round platform in the water, facing the gate, **knock it down with the Slingshot** and grab the Gold Skulltula Token.

items.name: Back room
items.desc:
On the first basement floor of the Deku Tree, after the Gohma Larvae room, light a Deku Stick on the torch and **burn the web on the back wall**. Behind it is a tunnel that ends at a wall of vines.

Watch out for the Big Skulltula guarding it: wait for it to turn around and strike its back. Then **knock the Gold Skulltula down with the Slingshot** and climb the vines up to the Gold Skulltula Token.
items.hint: You can get it on your first visit.

items.name: Heart Container - Gohma
items.desc:
After beating the three Deku Scrubs in the order 2, 3, 1, you can enter Queen Gohma's room on the second basement floor, and as soon as you go in, look up at the ceiling, because the boss drops down from there.

**When her eye turns red, shoot it with the Slingshot** or throw a Deku Nut to stun her, then hit her eye with your sword or a Deku Stick. If she climbs to the ceiling to lay eggs, break them before the larvae hatch. When she falls, she leaves the Heart Container.
items.hint: A Slingshot shot to the eye also knocks her down from the ceiling.

items.name: Behind the Baby Dodongos' wall
items.desc:
After dealing with the Beamos, blow up the cracked wall on the right side of the main hall with a Bomb Flower and you'll enter the Baby Dodongo corridor, with another cracked wall on the right as soon as you start.

Open it with a Bomb or **lure a Baby Dodongo over and kill it right up against the wall**, since its explosion breaks it too.

Inside are some Keese and the Gold Skulltula.
items.hint: It shares a corridor with the one on the Scarecrow's ledge.

items.name: Vines on the big staircase
items.desc:
The big staircase in the left wing, in the room full of Bomb Flowers, doesn't come down until you place the loose Bomb Flower in the gap in the row so they all go off in a chain, so start there.

Go up the stairs, climb the ladder and follow the ledge to the door at the back. Before you reach it there's **a climbable mesh wall with a regular Skulltula and the gold one**: take out both with the Slingshot (as an adult, with the Fairy Bow or the Hookshot) and climb up for the Gold Skulltula Token.

items.name: Pillar surrounded by Dodongos
items.desc:
On the first floor, as you leave the Bomb Bag chest room, blow up the cracked wall with a Bomb and keep going to the ledge overlooking the central room. There's another cracked wall there near the giant skull: **open it with a Bomb and go into that cave full of Dodongos**.

The Gold Skulltula is on a rock pillar in the middle of the room, surrounded by Dodongos. Dodge them or take them out, and knock the Skulltula down with your sword to claim the Gold Skulltula Token.
items.hint: Your sword is enough: you can get it on your first visit.

items.name: Armos room past the mouth
items.desc:
From the bridge on the second floor, drop a Bomb into each eye of the giant skull in the main hall so it opens its mouth, and go in through it. Pass the Fire Keese room and go up to the block corridor.

Push the blocks to climb onto the wooden beams and drop down into the fenced-off area at the back. There, **open the cracked wall with Bombs** and follow the tunnel. An Armos awaits, waking up as you approach, and the Gold Skulltula is on the wall behind it.

items.name: Scarecrow's ledge
items.desc:
As an adult, having already learned the Scarecrow's Song, go back to the Baby Dodongo corridor, the same one as the Skulltula behind the wall. Stay near the start of the corridor, facing a high ledge on the wall.

There, **play the Scarecrow's Song so Pierre appears on the ledge**: Hookshot over to him, climb up, kill the Gold Skulltula with your sword and grab the Gold Skulltula Token.
items.hint: With the Longshot you don't need the Scarecrow.

items.name: Heart Container - King Dodongo
items.desc:
You don't need the Boss Key to enter King Dodongo's lair: after the Armos cave, go back to the block room and push one onto the big floor switch to open the barred door. In the next room, break the pots, which hold Bombs, and **blow up the cracked patch of floor to drop down**.

Every time it opens its mouth to breathe in, throw a Bomb inside and, once it's stunned, lay into it with your sword. If it curls up and rolls, step aside or block with your shield, and grab the Heart Container before stepping into the blue warp.
items.hint: If you run out of Bombs, the room's Bomb Flowers will do.

items.name: Water switch room
items.desc:
Drop down the same hole as Ruto and follow the basement rooms to the one with the pool and the water switch. The Gold Skulltula is on the wall, in a nook at the top of the vines, above a ledge with three pots.

**Leave Ruto sitting on the switch so the water rises**. Swim to the vines, climb up to the ledge and kill the Skulltula with your sword to claim the Gold Skulltula Token.
items.hint: Ruto has to stay on the switch for the water to rise.

items.name: Basement of the big room, lower one
items.desc:
With the Boomerang in hand, go back to the big room with the holes where you met Ruto. Once the green tentacle is defeated, the pillar covering its hole, at the back on the right, pulls away: **drop down that hole**, throwing Ruto down first if you're carrying her.

Jellyfish drift around below, and there are two Gold Skulltulas on two adjoining walls; this is the lower one. Since you can't lock on to them, aim the Boomerang manually: it knocks it down and brings you the Gold Skulltula Token on the way back.
items.hint: You get it together with its partner above.

items.name: Basement of the big room, upper one
items.desc:
Below the big room with the holes, in the basement you drop into through the hole the green tentacle was covering, there are two Gold Skulltulas on adjoining walls, to the north and northwest. We recommend getting both at once, since they both need the Boomerang.

The one you're after here is the upper one, so **aim the Boomerang at it manually**, since you can't lock on to it either, and when it falls throw it again to bring back the Gold Skulltula Token.

items.name: Vines before the boss
items.desc:
You reach the room before Barinade from the dungeon's second room, the one with the pit that drops you down when you jump into it, by carrying a crate to the switch that opens the door.

First clear out the electric jellyfish with the Boomerang and look for the **column of vines that climbs toward the crystal switch**: the Gold Skulltula is on it. Kill it with the Boomerang and climb up to grab the Gold Skulltula Token.

items.name: Heart Container - Barinade
items.desc:
Barinade's door, at the back of the vine room, is locked by a switch protected by a crystal: climb the wall, lock on to the switch and **throw the Boomerang so it curves around behind it**.

Once inside, use the Boomerang to cut the three tentacles tying it to the ceiling, dodging the electric shocks, and finish off the jellyfish it releases. Then stun it with the Boomerang and hit it with your sword, repeat with the second wave of jellyfish, and don't step into the blue warp without grabbing the Heart Container first.

items.name: Entrance vines
items.desc:
The temple's first room is out in the open, with two trees and a pair of Wolfos that come at you, and the Gold Skulltula waits up high, near the Small Key chest.

Take out the Wolfos, **climb the vines on the right to the top of the tree** and, from the branch, kill it with the Hookshot (the Fairy Bow or a Bomb also work); the Hookshot itself brings you the Gold Skulltula Token.

items.name: Central hall
items.desc:
After the Poe Sisters cutscene you reach the central hall, the big room with the four torches and the elevator. This Gold Skulltula waits to the right of the stairs by the door opposite.

**Go up those stairs and turn right** to see it high on the wall, kill it with the Hookshot and fire it again to bring back the Gold Skulltula Token.
items.hint: Look carefully behind the walls.

items.name: Balcony above the stained-glass door
items.desc: From the landing by the stained-glass door, in the area where the water channel comes out, in the Forest Temple, you need to play the Scarecrow's Song: Pierre appears on the small balcony above the door. **Hookshot over to him**, kill the Gold Skulltula on the balcony floor and grab the Gold Skulltula Token.
items.hint: Pierre only appears if you play the Scarecrow's Song.

items.name: West courtyard ledge
items.desc:
Once you've straightened the twisted corridor and taken the Boss Key, drop through the hole in that room's floor to the water room below, go up its stairs and come out onto the stone walkway high above the west courtyard.

At the end of the walkway, just before the door, **drop down to the mossy stone platform on the left**. Look up: the Gold Skulltula is on the wall, ready for the Hookshot, which also brings you the Gold Skulltula Token. With the Longshot you can reach it from the courtyard floor.
items.hint: Look to the top of the stone wall.

items.name: Rotating room in the basement
items.desc:
With the four Poe Sisters defeated, the elevator in the central hall takes you down to the basement, a room of rotating walls that leads to the boss door.

You don't need to move the walls for this Gold Skulltula: **follow the circular corridor as soon as you step off the elevator and go into the open alcove with the pots**. A Big Skulltula drops from the ceiling; finish it off and look high on the wall, where the gold one waits. Knock it down with the Hookshot, which also brings you the Gold Skulltula Token.
